To express the number in Cartesian form, we expand the parentheses and substitute the values of the cosine and sine.

First, we find $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3}) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\,,\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3}) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the values and expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =6\sqrt{3}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})) \\  & =6\sqrt{3}(-\frac{1}{2}-\text{i}\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{6\sqrt{3}}{2}-\text{i}\,\frac{18}{2} \\  & =-3\sqrt{3}-9\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$
